name: chromosomix
description: Genome browser for Hi-C and Micro-C contact maps, genome tracks and 3D models, and the command line that runs its analyses: insulation, compartments, loops, APA, P(s) and more.
author: Jacques Serizay

scripts.build:desktop: npm run typecheck && vite build --config vite.desktop.config.ts && tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json && node scripts/build-preload.mjs && node scripts/check-desktop-build.mjs
scripts.dist:desktop: npm run build:desktop && electron-builder --config electron-builder.config.cjs --publish never && node scripts/check-package.mjs
scripts.preversion: npm run typecheck && npm run test:nofixtures
scripts.build:cli: npm run typecheck && vite build --config vite.cli.config.ts
scripts.build:standalone: npm run typecheck && vite build --config vite.standalone.config.ts && node scripts/check-standalone-build.mjs
scripts.build:package: npm run build:cli && vite build --config vite.package.config.ts && node scripts/check-package-build.mjs

comments.dependencies: What `npm install -g chromosomix` installs, so only what a file in the package imports when it runs: the three the CLI's bundle leaves external (vite.cli.config.ts), and nothing else. Everything a bundle compiles in is a devDependency, `echarts` and `three` among them — `dist/` already carries both, and the command line loads neither. Declared here they were 90 MB of the 116 MB an install of the package put on disk (SPECS §22.2).
comments.three: The one library that draws in three dimensions (§25), and a devDependency for the reason `dependencies` gives. Everything else on screen is a `CanvasRenderingContext2D`, hand-written down to the PDF, and the argument for that was never *no dependencies* but *not for this arithmetic*: an eighty-line PDF writer beats a library that does the same sums. A lit tube of ten thousand beads under an orbiting camera, with instanced spheres, fat lines, sorted transparency and raycast picking, is not that arithmetic, and three.js is the smallest library that has all five. It draws the structure cell of a deck and nothing else: the map, the tracks and every figure export stay on the 2D context. **Pinned exactly**, as `electron` is and for the same reason: three.js breaks something every release, and a floating range would change the renderer under an `npm ci`. Bumping it is a CHANGELOG `Changed` entry. The site build splits it into its own chunk, loaded on the first structure opened; the standalone file inlines it (§19), which is the measured cost recorded there.
comments.@types/three: The types for the pin above, at the same version, and for no other reason.
comments.g3djs: A devDependency, and the oracle `test/unit/g3d-binary-oracle.test.ts` reads the fixtures with — never a runtime dependency, on `hic-straw`'s argument exactly: every read in this app goes through a source that counts its requests, caches its chunks and signs them where a bucket needs it, and a parser that fetches for itself sits outside all three. The binary `.g3d` reader is written here (`src/annotations/g3dBinary.ts`); what a second implementation buys is the one thing a round trip against our own writer cannot, which is a reading of the container that this repository did not make. Installed with `--ignore-scripts`, because a transitive dependency of it still calls `node-waf`, which has not existed for a decade; nothing that runs in the oracle needs the script.
comments.test:nofixtures: Everything that does not need test/fixtures/, which are generated by `npm run fixtures` and need a Python interpreter with metacooler installed. This is what a fresh clone and a CI runner without metacooler can verify; `npm test` is the full suite and is what to run before a release. Of the request budgets (SPECS §12) only `requests.test.ts` is left out, because it opens the metacool fixtures: `alignments.test.ts` builds its BAM in memory and `analysis.test.ts` reads committed demo data, and excluding the whole directory once hid a red budget from CI for weeks.
comments.overrides: This host runs glibc 2.28 (RHEL 8); rollup's native binding requires GLIBC_2.29 and fails to dlopen. @rollup/wasm-node is rollup's own drop-in for unsupported platforms. Slower to build, identical output. Remove this override on a host with glibc >= 2.29.
comments.version: The version this bundle reports. `npm version <patch|minor|major>` is the whole release: it runs the checks, refuses a version CHANGELOG.md does not mention, commits, and tags. Pushing the tag is what publishes, since GitHub Pages builds every push to main.
comments.files: What a tarball contains, and the whole of what stands between a publish and 250 MB of yeast Hi-C. `demo/` is data, `test/fixtures/` is generated, `src/` is the thing `dist/` is built from — and npm's default is *everything not gitignored*, so the failure this prevents is one command with no flag on it. Two directories go: `dist/`, the viewer, built by `build:package` for a relative base so it runs from whatever path it is unpacked into; and `dist-cli/`, so the `bin` below resolves to a file that is actually in the package rather than to a broken symlink on somebody's PATH. This replaces `private: true`, whose comment argued that an application is not a library and that there is nothing here a registry would want. The first half is still true and the second was about the wrong thing: what a registry is wanted for here is not dependency resolution, it is *hosting nobody has to trust* — an immutable, checksummed, mirrored copy of one version of the viewer that a page can frame or a site can vendor without depending on this project's own domain staying up. A distribution channel beside GitHub Pages, rather than a library.
comments.icons:stores: Fits IGV's, 4DN's and ENCODE's own logos to the square a store tile draws, into src/ui/stores/logos.generated.ts as data URIs. Reads IGV.png, 4DN.png and ENCODE.png from the repository root, which are supplied by hand and are NOT committed — the generated file is the artefact of record, so re-running means putting the three back first, and the script says so by name if they are missing. Fitting is the point: a tile draws with `object-fit: cover`, and ENCODE's badge is far wider than it is tall, so used raw it would be cropped to the middle of the helix with the wordmark gone. Rerun after replacing a logo, and commit what changes.
comments.icons:rsg: Draws the lab's two store marks into src/ui/stores/rsg-mark.generated.ts and dbz-mark.generated.ts: a Hi-C map 100 bins square whose diagonal spells RSG, and a bacterial one — circular, its arms zipped into an X — whose diagonal spells DBZ, each as an indexed PNG data URI whose palette is the viewer's own `default` ramp. Committed, and needs nothing but Node, so a fresh clone and a CI runner both have the mark without running anything. They are the two shipped stores whose logos are the lab's own; the others carry their projects' published logos, fitted by scripts/make-store-logos.mjs. Rerun after editing scripts/make-rsg-mark.mjs, and commit what changes.
comments.icons:app: Draws every icon the app has, in the dark variant, from one description of the mark: public/icon-192.png and icon-512.png for the install prompt, public/apple-touch-icon.png for the iOS home screen, build/icon.png at 1024 for electron-builder to derive every platform icon from, and index.html's favicon, which the script rewrites in place. All committed, because they are build inputs rather than build output and neither a fresh clone nor a CI runner has Pillow. Needs `pip install pillow numpy`, and takes METACOOLER_PYTHON the way `fixtures` does. Rerun after editing scripts/make-app-icons.py, and commit what changes.
comments.main: The Electron entry point, and it points into a build directory rather than at a source file: `electron/main.cts` compiles to CommonJS because this package is `type: module` and Electron's main process cannot be ESM. Meaningless to the web build, which has no entry point of its own -- index.html is the entry point there. Meaningless to a registry consumer, and it cannot simply be dropped: `electron .` reads it, so the desktop target needs it and the tarball has no use for it. npm **force-includes the file `main` names**, ahead of `files` and ahead of a negation — `"!dist-electron"` was tried and changes nothing — so 18 KB of compiled main process rides along with any pack run in a working tree that has built the desktop target. Inert, since nothing in the package requires it, but it makes the tarball depend on local state. Which is the reason to publish from CI, or from a clean clone, where `dist-electron/` does not exist: see .github/workflows/release.yml.
comments.electron: Pinned exactly, not caret-ranged. This is the browser the desktop user runs, so a floating range would silently change the rendering engine under a `npm ci`. Bumping it is a CHANGELOG `Changed` entry for the same reason. Track the latest three majors, which is the window Electron itself supports.
comments.@gmod/bam: A devDependency, and the oracle `test/unit/bam-oracle.test.ts` reads the fixtures with -- never a runtime dependency. `annotations/bam/format.ts` records why the reader is written here instead: every read in this app goes through a source that counts its requests, caches its chunks and signs them where a bucket needs it, and a parser that fetches for itself sits outside all three. The same argument, and the same arrangement, as `hic-straw`. What a second implementation buys is the only thing a round-trip against our own writer cannot: a mutual misunderstanding of the record layout round-trips perfectly and opens in nothing -- which is exactly the bug it caught on its first run.
comments.engines: The floor is Electron 43's now, not Vite's. The `^20.19.0` half had to go: it satisfies Vite and vitest, but cannot run the desktop toolchain, so leaving it in would have advertised a Node version on which half the scripts fail.
comments.build:pinned: The archived copy of one commit, built to be served from `<base>v/<commit>/` and published beside the site by .github/workflows/deploy.yml — or, under `<base>pr/<number>/`, the preview of a pull request that .github/workflows/preview.yml publishes the same way. Needs PINNED_BASE and refuses to build without it, because the base contains a commit hash and there is nothing to guess. Same source, no service worker, no manifest, no demo data and no source maps — about 5 MB, which is what makes keeping twenty of them affordable inside the 1 GB Pages budget. Then it asserts the shape of what came out, because every way that shape goes wrong is both silent and late: an archived build is what nobody opens for months.
comments.build:desktop: A second invocation of the bundler, never a change to the first. `build` is the command line .github/workflows/deploy.yml runs and it must keep working byte-for-byte; this one reads the same source through vite.desktop.config.ts, compiles the main process, and then asserts the shape of what came out, because every way that shape goes wrong is silent.
comments.dist:desktop: Builds the installers. Deliberately *not* part of `preversion`: `npm version patch` would otherwise download a 100 MB Electron binary and pack a .dmg to bump a number. In CI this is what .github/workflows/release.yml runs, once per platform, when a GitHub release is *created* — a tag alone does not mean 'ship binaries'.
comments.fixtures:scool: The single-cell containers, and the only fixture command that needs nothing but `cooler` — `make_fixtures` drives the private metacooler CLI over a test-data directory only a metacooler checkout has, and none of the scool fixtures want it. Split out so a contributor with `pip install cooler` alone can build and run the scool suite; `fixtures` runs it too. The standard container comes from `cooler.create_scool`, the flat one is restructured from that output because no maintained tool writes that layout any more — see the script's docstring, which records what it was checked against.
comments.fixtures:hicpro: The HiC-Pro pairs, and like `fixtures:scool` it needs only `cooler`. It writes them *from* a cooler — HiC-Pro is a pipeline that starts at FASTQ and cannot be driven here, and the format it outputs is four lines of documentation — which makes the test stronger rather than weaker: the manifest carries cooler's own dense matrix, so the JS suite asserts that the two text files mean exactly the matrix they were written from. All four `MATRIX_FORMAT` variants are written, because all four must land on the same picture and only one of them is the common case.
comments.fixtures:analysis: The oracles the Analysis tasks are checked against (SPECS §18.10), from cooltools and friends over the published demo data rather than from the synthetic fixtures. A second command and not a flag on `fixtures`: the two prove different layers, against different references, to different bars, and they need different packages — folding them together would mean a run that half-succeeds on a machine missing one of them. Needs `pip install cooler cooltools coolpuppy pyBigWig` (chromosight, and R with HiContacts, for the goldens that ask for them); every golden it cannot build is named in its manifest rather than quietly omitted, because an absent golden and an unwritten one look identical from the JS side. The peak caller's three — yapc, its pipeline with IDR, and IDR alone — are the exception to one environment: yapc 0.1 and IDR 2.0.3 install only under numpy < 1.24 and Cython < 3, so they are built in a venv of their own, which the script's section on them sets out, with `npm run fixtures:analysis -- --only yapc yapc_idr idr`, and every other golden is left as it was.
comments.build:cli: The Analysis panel as a shell command (GAPS G4). A fourth invocation of the same bundler over the same source, never an edit to the first: `RUNNERS`, `MetaCooler` and the writers are imported, so a number computed in a batch and a number computed by clicking come out of one implementation with one set of goldens behind it. `h5wasm` and `@gmod/bbi` stay external because both ship assets a single file cannot carry, which is why they are `dependencies` rather than dev ones: a published package installs them, and `npx chromosomix` then works from a registry the way it works from a clone.
comments.bin: Declared so `npm link` and a workspace install put `chromosomix` on the PATH, and — since `files` includes `dist-cli/` — so that `npx chromosomix` works against a published version with no clone at all. `h5wasm` and `@gmod/bbi` are `dependencies` rather than dev ones for exactly this reason: the bundle keeps them external, so npm has to have installed them by the time the command runs.
comments.build:standalone: One HTML file that opens from a disk and works — for an air-gapped machine, a reviewer who will not install anything, and a locked-down laptop holding unpublished data. A fifth reading of the same source, never an edit to the first. Four things a file:// page forbids decide the whole config: no module workers, no sibling fetch, no network, no service worker. Then the shape is asserted, because a build that kept module workers looks completely normal until somebody drops a file on it.
comments.build:package: The sixth reading of the same source, and the only one built for a path it does not know. Everything else this repository emits is served from somewhere decided in advance — the site root, `/v/<commit>/`, an asar, a disk — and bakes absolute asset URLs accordingly. A tarball is unpacked into a lab site, a course page, an institutional server or a registry CDN, so its base is `./` and one published version serves all of them with no rebuild. Then the shape is asserted, because `dist/` is written by two builds and only one of them may be published, and because a wrong tarball cannot be taken back the way a wrong deploy can.
comments.prepack: Runs before `npm pack` and before `npm publish`, so what is packed is built from source at that moment rather than being whatever happened to be in `dist/`. Not belt and braces: `npm run build` writes to the same directory for the *site*, with absolute asset URLs and 20 MB of source maps, and a tarball packed over one of those would 404 on every mount that is not the site root. `prepack` rather than `prepublishOnly`, because `npm pack` has to produce the identical tarball — it is how anybody checks what a publish would send.
comments.fixtures:pairs: The `cooler cload pairs` oracle for the .pairs importer (SPECS §3.7), and the condition §18.9's narrowing was granted on: writing a contact matrix is permitted for the primary reduction of a primary file, and the bar for that is a golden built from the reference implementation's own output rather than from a previous run of this code. A third command and not a flag on `fixtures`, for the same reason `fixtures:analysis` is one — different layer, different reference, different packages, and folding them together would mean a run that half-succeeds on a machine missing one of them. Needs `pip install cooler`; `bgzip` and `pairix` are used when present and skipped when not, since the importer reads a plain file and the index is opportunistic. `test/unit/pairs-cload-oracle.test.ts` skips by name when the golden is absent, which is what a fresh clone and a CI runner see.
comments.fixtures:pairstats: The `pairtools stats` oracle for the counts the .pairs import makes (SPECS §3.7): a fixture of 30,300 records drawn from the yeast Micro-C cooler with every pair type pairtools writes, and pairtools' own `.stats` for it, both under test/golden/pairs_stats/ and both committed, so test/unit/pairs-stats.test.ts runs on every push with nothing to build. Needs pairtools 1.1.2 and h5py, under Python 3.12 or older — pairtools imports the `pipes` module 3.13 removed — so it is run with an interpreter of its own: `uv venv -p 3.12 .venv-pairtools && uv pip install -p .venv-pairtools pairtools==1.1.2 h5py`, then `METACOOLER_PYTHON=.venv-pairtools/bin/python npm run fixtures:pairstats`.
comments.fixtures:restriction: The restriction-digest oracles (src/genome/restriction.ts): `bioframe.digest` of demo/yeast/S288c_syn40-XIII.fa for every preset enzyme and two typed sites, `pairtools restrict` over the pairs-stats fixture with the DpnII fragments of each strand, and the fragment statistics computed from restrict's columns, all under test/golden/restriction/ and committed, so the restriction tests run on every push with nothing to build. bioframe's boundaries are two bases past the true cut (Biopython reports the first base after it and bioframe adds one), and the script's docstring says how the goldens allow for it. Needs the interpreter `fixtures:pairstats` uses with bioframe and Biopython added: `uv pip install -p .venv-pairtools bioframe==0.8.0 biopython==1.88`, then `METACOOLER_PYTHON=.venv-pairtools/bin/python npm run fixtures:restriction`.
comments.fixtures:g3d: The binary g3d containers the structure reader is held to (SPECS §25), written by `g3dtools load` itself over a text model this script lays out deterministically — so the file `src/annotations/g3dBinary.ts` is tested against is one the reference tool produced, and `test/unit/g3d-binary-oracle.test.ts` reads it with both the in-house reader and the `g3djs` package, bead for bead at every resolution. A separate command for the reason `fixtures:scool` is one: it needs only `pip install g3dtools`, which brings the `msgpack` the decoder's round-trip case is packed with, and nothing else here wants it. The oracle test and the msgpack round trip skip by name when the fixtures are absent, which is what a fresh clone and a CI runner see.
comments.fixtures:demo: The four published demo maps — a .metacool and an .mmetacool metacooler wrote, a yeast .cool and an E. coli .mcool — put in test/fixtures/demo/ for test/unit/demo-maps.test.ts, checked against the size and MD5 test/golden/demo/_manifest.json records. Copied from demo/ when an identical copy is there, which costs no network; `-- --from s3` fetches them from the lab's public bucket instead, which is what the golden job does so that it proves the bucket still serves what the goldens were made from. Needs nothing but Node: this is the reader oracle a runner without metacooler can still run.
comments.fixtures:demo-golden: Rebuilds test/golden/demo/ from the demo maps with the public cooler package alone (`pip install cooler`): binsize, shape, the sequence table as a hash, every genome's extent from /indexes/genome_offset, and small windows across the diagonal, a seam, both orientations between two sequences and between two genomes. Committed, like every golden; rerun after a demo map changes, and the golden job reruns it to check the committed files are still what cooler reads. `-- --maps <dir>` reads the maps from a directory instead of demo/.
comments.demo:hub: The demo track hub (SPECS §24.10), and the files the UCSC readers need to be tried on rather than only reasoned about. Writes a real **assembly hub** over `demo/yeast/` — the genome packed as a `.2bit`, the loop calls as `longrange`, the six bigWigs as a composite and the contact map as `type hic` — so `npm run dev` and `http://localhost:5173/demo/yeast/hub.txt` walk the whole path same-origin, with no third-party host and no CORS question in the way. Needs nothing installed to run; `pip install py2bit` adds the check that matters, which reads the `.2bit` back with the C in kent's own tree and compares every base against the FASTA — a file this repository wrote and this repository read proves only that two implementations share a reading of the format, which is exactly what they would do if the reading were wrong. Idempotent, and committed output: the files it writes are demo data like the rest of that directory.
comments.store: The store generator (SPECS §24.3) — and the one Python script here that needs **nothing installed**: `urllib`, `json` and `xml.etree`, so a weekly workflow and a contributor with a bare interpreter run the identical command. No `METACOOLER_PYTHON`, unlike every `fixtures:*` above, because those drive the private metacooler CLI over a test-data directory and this drives a portal over HTTPS. Pass the front end after `--`: `npm run store -- 4dn --out out/4dn.json` and `npm run store -- encode --out out/encode.json` ask the 4DN and ENCODE search APIs for every released contact map and join each file to the cell line, assay, assembly and lab that name it — the join a browser cannot do for itself and should not try on a reader's first click; `npm run store -- bucket https://my-lab.s3.amazonaws.com/hic/ --name 'Lab Hi-C' --out store.json` walks a prefix with `ListObjectsV2` and lists whatever this viewer has a route for, which is the `make_catalog.py` GAPS G10 promised. `--check` re-reads a written store and validates it against the contract `src/state/store.ts` parses, because a store that is valid JSON and wrong publishes, parses and draws an empty table; a run that found nothing exits 2, so .github/workflows/stores.yml can tell an empty catalogue from a portal outage and leave the published shelf alone. The two built-in stores the picker offers are that workflow's output rather than this command's: running it by hand is for a lab's own bucket, or for seeing what next Monday will publish.
